articleTitle: Method of Signal Extrapolation Applied to Cancel Impulsive Noise in the Communication Systems
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In some cases it is necessary to cancel impulsive noise appearing in radiocommunication systems intended for various purposes. This noise may include man-made noise occurring in mobile service systems and pulses generated by radio facilities making use of pulse modulations generally employed in the radio-relay communication systems. The paper presents the results obtained by a new method used to cancel such noise in the analogue communication systems. The relations characterizing the efficiency of the method and affording to determine optimum parameters for the devices realizing this method are also given.

articleTitle: Automated System of EMC Examination of VHF Radio Sets for Individual Computers
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A system of the software and data base for EMC examination, which is developed in BASIC language for an individual computer, is presented.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigations of Mutual Effect of Small-Size Antennas Located on a Circular Cylinder
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Problems of small-size antennas optimal location on a circular cylinder are touched upon, with which the best conditions of their electromagnetic compatibility are realized. Results of experimental investigations for determination of the character of small-size antennas decoupling change depending on the angle and separation, on the type of interacting radiators and their mutual orientation are presented. Potentialities of EMC improvement by the change of interacting antennas type and orientation are found out. A number of practical recommendations on antennas optimal location on objects which shape may be approximated by a cylinder is formulated.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of Antenna Coupling Coefficients
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The isolation increase between antennas may be achieved at the expense of the special choice of amplitude-phase distribution in antenna apertures. To analyze antenna array coupling coefficients a matrix model of interaction has been proposed, and design relations based on it have been obtained. A general problem has been formulated and a number of specific problems of antenna array parameter optimization have been solved taking into consideration the isolation requirements. The design procedures are given and the theoretical results are verified by the data of the experiment.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Estimation of the Minimum Necessary Number of Transmitters Network Channels
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Results of investigations of the multiplex local optimization accuracy for estimation of the minimum necessary channels number in the problem of frequency planning of N transmitters network at the uniform frequency spectrum are presented in the paper. High accuracy of the multiplex local optimization in problems of the medium dimension is shown (N=50+100). Comparative 0estimation of accuracy of different approach to determination of the required channels number are presented.

articleTitle: Radio Interference Prediction in Switching Transistor Converters
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To predict radio interference in switching transistor converters used in electronic apparatus feeders the method is suggested which allows to calculate radio interference levels at input and output terminals of a device, depending on parameters of basic active and passive elements, spurious parameters of circuit and structure elements, the effects of primary mains as well as loading on the converter. Experimental investigations confirmed the high accuracy of the suggested method. The application of the prediction method makes it possible to evaluate the SMC indices of switching transistor converters at the design stage.

articleTitle: Algorithms of the Electromagnetic Intereference Classification
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Methods of discrimination of narrowband and broadband electromagnetic interference on the base of spectrum classification by methods of cepstrum and excess processing are considered in the paper. Probability criterion of the pulse and fluctuation interference discrimination is also considered.

articleTitle: Determining Pulse Disturbances Amplitude in Testing Digital Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This article presents a method of theoretical defining of the minimum amplitude of pulse diturbances in the testing process the susceptibility of digital electronic divices to disturbances occurring in low voltage power systems. The maximum permissible deviation of the power sypply for different digital integrated circuits has been chosen as a criterion. The theoretical analysis has been made for differetial and common mode disturbances.

articleTitle: Properties of Digital Equipments EMI Field
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There are several sources radiate from electronic equipment. In each case the equivalent radiation source may be analysed as the perfect conductiong plane. Such antenna as the sum of electric and magnetic dipoles is considered in the paper.

articleTitle: Selection of Parameters for Description of Summary Man-Made Noise in the Information System
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Some results of summary man-made noise are presented which are necessary for projecting of the information system data base, The measuring complex consisting of broadband measuring antennas, CISPR RFI measuring sets and an analyzer of random processes is described. Investigations of man-made noise are carried out in the frequency range from 0,15 to 500MHz, in the city conditions in residential buildings, on building rooves, in open space.

articleTitle: Statistical Investigations of the Effective Frequency Assignment Methods for Radiocommunication Facilities of the Metric Band
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper results of the computer statistical investigation of the effective frequency assignment methods for radiocommunication facilities of the metric band are presented. It's shown that in the given frequency-space resource the number of satisfied requists before the primary refusal in the radio facilities frequency assignment is described best of all with the help of probabilities beta-distribution. The methods preference order is determined.

articleTitle: Impulse Technique of Measurement of Magnetic and Elecrtic Coupling
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Short time voltage transients Induce pulse voltages in control cables and shipboard equipment circuits, it is important to know coupling of cables and circuits.

articleTitle: Procedure of Analytical Evaluation of Rain Scatter Interference Level between Radioelectronic Systems
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the report is presented the procedure of obtaining the determinate analitical evalution of the rain scatter interference level between radioelectronic systems. The procedure is based on approximating expressions for the results of the numerical calculations of the reflectivity matrix elements(Mueller's matrix). The approximating expression of the reflectivity matrix may be useful in the theoretical studies of various effects which are concerned with the radiowave scattering by rain.

articleTitle: Methods of Estimation of Lightning Velocity and Equivalent Impedance by Means of Analysis ITS Quasi-Linear Partial Differential Equations
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility

articleTitle: Consideration on the Receiving Methods Unification and Presentation forms of Man-Made Noise and on the Creation of the Information System
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: General principles of the data base creation of an information system for man-made noise are suggested. Purposes of the system creation are considered as well as contents and form of the storing information necessary for solution of man-made noise problems, the most important of which is analysis of operation quality of different radio networks in conditions of the man-made noise action.

articleTitle: Simulation of Frequency Planning Algorithms and its Software
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The task of experimental comparison of heuristic algorithms of frequency planning for the set of space-dispersed transmitters is considered. The description of a simulation experiment, a software package structure and a data base is given.

articleTitle: Observations of the Low Frequencu Electromagnetic Emissions in the Upper Ionosphere over Earthquake Areas
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An anomalous increase in the intensity of low-frequency emissions (0,1-16 kHz) was detected from Intercosmos 19 and 18 during the satellitens flights near the earthquake epicentre. On the basis of ample statistical data the probabilistic spatial-temporal dimensions of the area are obtained for the altitudes of the upper ionosphere where seismic-related ELF-VLF emissions were detected. The interpretation of the results is given.

articleTitle: VLF Mission Observations in Field -Aligned Currents Region
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: At the ionospheric hights the VLF emission intensity at frequencies 140Hz-15000 Hz and three magnetic field components on board the satellite "Intercosmos-18" were measured. The near-earth plasma is inhomogeneous. It is characterized by gradients of magnetic field, temperature and particle flux density variations. Local instabilities therefore c/o originate, resulting in formation of oscillations and waves of different types withing wide range of frequencies. Simultaneous email-scale variations of magnetic field components and VLF emmissions in the field-aligned current region in the south polar cusp are revealed. The possible sources of simultaneous variations originating are discussed. The paper is devoted to the experimental confirmation the possibility of VLF excitation by small-scale field-aligned currents.

articleTitle: Designing of Interference Suppressing Filters for Switching Transistor Converters
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A technique of RF switching transistor converters filters synthesis is suggested. The technique makes it possible to take into account basic and spurious parameters of filters elements and to ensure the filters matching necessary for converters normal operation. The filters calculated by the suggested technique allow to reduce converter interference levels to the corresponding limiting value, to have the best mass-overall dimension and power factors. Experimental in vestigation of the filters characteristics shows high accuracy of the suggested technique.

articleTitle: Proposed Simplifications to the Log-Normal Method for an Assessment of Usable Field Strength
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Some simplifications to the log-normal method of multiple interference assessment used for planning of sound and TV broadcasting networks are proposed. The simplified calculation procedure reduces the amount of computations while maintaining accuracy of the results obtained. Analysis of the results of calculations shows that the proposed procedure pro - vides intermediate values as compared to the results obtained by the simplified multiplication method and power sum method which are most frequently used at present.

articleTitle: The Estimation of the Effect of Limits Establishing for Immunity Parameters on the Quality of Operation of Mobile Communication Service Receivers
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The estimation of the effect of limits establishing for immunity of mobile communication receivers is performed. The assumption is made that each receiver in a certain moment of time is subjected by the influence of a single, sufficiently powerfull, interference source. On this basis the criterion of electromagnetic incompatibility before and after limits establishing for immunity parameters is calculated. It is shown that the introduction of stringent limits may prove to be unreasonable, since in that case the criterion of electromagnetic incompatibility seems to be poorly dependent on the limits adopted. This circumstance should be taken into account while developing immunity limits.

articleTitle: The Reduction of Coupling between Slot Antennas by Means of Absorber and a Longitudinal Wire Frame
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper gives the results of the experimental study of decoupling slot antennas by means of an absorbing layer, covering a part of conducting surface between antennas, and rectangular wire frame, oriented along a connction line and laying in the plane perpendicular to the absorber surface. This plane is also the plane of polarizing an electric field. In the paper there are given the data characterizing the influence of wire frame dimensions upon the attenuation value. The results of investigating the properties of a combined decoupling system are also given in the paper. It was revealed that total value of decoupling exceeds 40 dB, that is considerably more than than the field attenuation caused separately by every element forming the combined system.

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of Magnetic Field Coupling to Multiple Feed Back Band Pass Filter
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The magnetic fields (H-field) associated with functioning of generators and power supplies couple to cable loops and circuits and as a result of this, sensitive electronic systems are up-set leading to erroneous outputs. The problem will be more severe when the magnetic field couples to the input end of high gain, sensitive and low-noise electronic circuits. The undesired coupled voltage will at times override the actual signal causing catastrophic failures in the system. It is therefore necessary to understand the nature of magnetic field coupling to cable loops and various circuits of a system so as to enable the designers to take suitable control measures at the initial stage. In this paper, a computer analysis is made of the low frequency magnetic field coupling to a multiple feed back pass filter. (See : Figure 1). For the analysis, magnetic fields generated at various frequencies viz., 5 KHz, 20 KHz and 30 KHz of different wave shapes eg., square wave, sinusoidal wave and positive ramp wave (See : Figure 2) are considered. In the analysis, however, the fourier transforms for the above waveforms are obtained at 128 discrete multiples of fundamental frequencies and then the H-field coupling to the electronic circuit is evaluated taking into consideration the transfer functions of the cable loop and the band-pass filter. Finally, the inverse discrete fourier transform (IDFT) is taken to reconstruct the time-domain waveform of the coupled voltages. The various steps involved in the computer software analysis of the problem are given in the flow-chart form (See : Figure 3). To verify the simulation results, a circuit model of the band-pass filter is designed and has been subjected to the stress of uniform magnetic fields generated by means of a Helmholtzcoil setup (See: Figure 4). To generate the required magnetic fields, various signal waveform generators at the required frequencies are used in practice. The output of a signal generator is fed to an amplifier which inturn drives the Helmholtz coil. The designed circuit is placed on the turn-table associated with the Helmholtz coil setup and the coupled waveshapes are observed and then recorded.

articleTitle: Modelung a Multilayer Printed Circuit Board for Minimum Electromagnetic Radiation
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The moment method technique was used to determine the radiated electric fields for several layout trace configurations of a printed circuit board studied in an earlier work [1]. The layout which produces the minimum radiated fields was thereby obtained. Only a portion of clock trace from the board, the ground plane and reflecting plane were modelled using several straight round wires forming a radiating structure. Comparison of the radiated fields among the several layout configurations varied substantially and useful data was obtained to corroborate quantitatively some of the presently known guidelines used in the design and layout of printed circuit boards.

articleTitle: Solitary Travelling Ionospheric Disturbances in the Ionosphere F Region and their Influence on Fluctuations of VLF Radiosignals
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents results of theoretical and also numerical investigations of the solitary internal gravity wave (IGW) dynamice at heights of the ionosphere F region, their relationships with the F layer ionization and the influence exerted by travelling ionospheric disturbances (TID's) on the fluctuations of VLF radiosignals, propagating in ionospheric plasma and in earth-ionosphere waveguide.

articleTitle: A New Approach to the Possibility of the Signal Cables Magnetic Screening Research
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: V príspevku popisujeme možnosť použitia fólií z tzv. kovových skiel na magnetické tienenie oznamovacích káblov. Uvádzame skúsenosti s fóliami VITROVAC a VITROKOV. Ako porovnávací parameter sme použili redukčný faktor oznamovacieho kábla.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Influence of the Manufacturing Accuracy on the Microstrip Antenna Properties
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the influence of the manufacturing tolerances on the resonance frequency of a rectangular microstrip antenna is discused. First, the method of the uncertainty analysis for rectangular microstrip antennas is presented. Next, the results of the numerical modelling are shown. Finally, the suggestions arising from this analysis are discused.

articleTitle: Study of RF Coupling Behaviour of Digital Logic Devices
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper TTL, CMOS, STTL and HCMOS digital logic devices are studied for their functional characteristics towards HF, VHF and UHF frequencies. It has been identified that commonly used logic devices provide a very high gain RF coupling path particularly when used as terminal devices in data transmission lines. The uncertain characteristics of the gates at the transition region have been reported in this paper. Useful data concerning RF threshold levels, RF gain at the transition state for the logic families are included. Various methods to control the unwanted RF gain of these devices and their implications on the basic characteristics have been studied and also reported. The result of analysis can be used in the selection and application of these devices in strategic areas of data communication and signal processing.

articleTitle: Some Characteristics of the Natural Radionoise in the Frequency Range between 4 and 500HZ
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The naturally occuring electromagnetic Ez - radiation has been investigated. Measurements have been carried out in region of Magadan in the summer of 1986. All recording and receiving instruments were battery operated and a favourable signal-to-noise ratio has been obtained. The tape records were analyzed by a statistical spacial computer, which calculated the amplitude spectral density of ELF radionoise.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Stabilized Sights and Laser Range Finder in a Combat Vehicle
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive EMI/ EMC study of the stabilized sights for Commander & Gunner and Laser Range Finder (LRF) in a Combat vehicle. The EMI emission levels and EMI susceptibility thresholds of the LRF and stabilized sights are measured. The EMI/EMC evaluation results of the typical stabilized sights and LRF are critically analyzed. Finally, the EMI control methods, to achieve the electromagnetic compatibility of these sensitive subsystems in a small confine of a combat vehicle are also discussed for incorporation during the design stage.

articleTitle: Radio Noise and its Reduction in Modern Power Sources for Hand Electric ARC Welding
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The topic of this report is an analysis of the interference in the modern sources for hand electric arc welding. Radio noise interference and its reduction 1n frequency range from 10 kHz to 30 MHz is discussed. Semiconductor rectifiers and inverters are analysed as sources for electric arc welding. The reduction RFI by means of RFI filters.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Electrical Equipment and Automatic Control AIDS on Cargo Ships
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of the provision of the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) on cargo ships has arisen owing to the increase of malfunction of the electronic equipment (EE) due to the mutual electromagnetic effect of the shipboard technical facilities. Introduction of modern engineering electronics has resulted in new sources of interferences the levels of which are different for various ship's spaces and types of Ship's power-plants. As a criterion for the provision of the EMC there must serve the requirements for the EE susceptibility, the admissible norm values of which can be determined on the basis of the total pattern of the ship's electromagnetic situation.

articleTitle: A Continuation Method Applied to the Identification of Complex Natural Frecuencies of Radar Target
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work we apply a continuation method to extract the complex natural frequencies from the late-time electromagnetic field scattered from a finite sized conducting body. We propose an alternative form to carry out the correction stage, which presents important advantages with respect to the convergence and the computational time.

articleTitle: Investigation of Radiated Interference Stability of Digital Telephone Exchanges
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In switching technique, the really existing electromagnetic environment and the application of high sensitive micro-electronics, constrain to more consideration of EMC problems. Thereby, the Radio Frequency Interference of the devices is particulary problematic. Methodes are represented, making it possible to investigate the radiated susceptibility of given installations, excluding the influence by coupling into the cables outside the station. The very high functional complexity of exchanging equipment and their large dimensions in space, constrain to combinations of calculation and measuring methodes, apply to parts of the equipment, whereby the total reaction can be estimated. Conceptions are stated, how should be corrected the requirements to the installations concerning ingenious declarations for intensity and characteristics of the interfering signals, existing in the GDR standards, to make those standards more evident.

articleTitle: Analysis of N-Slot Structure Corrugated Horn
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: On the space harmonics technique the general formulas are derived of the characteristic equation and the equivalent wall admittance of corrugated horns with N-slot structure (each period has IT slots whose shape and depth may be same or different). As an example, the calculated radiation patterns for a corrugated horn having dual-depth corrugations show good agreement with the measured ones.

articleTitle: Some Notes on the Ultimate Accuracy of Parameter Measurements in Monitoring
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Recent developments in digital signal processing make the high-resolution and high-accurąpy monitoring feasible. One possible way to implement high-resolution monitoring is to use spectral-related methods to increase accuracy and selectivity. In such a system, the intermediate-frequency signal of the measuring receiver is appropriately converted to the band of an FFT analyzer and the selection and measurements of signals is performed on the baseband spectrum. In contrast to the analog solutions, digital methods offer very flexible arrangements. The selectivity for instance can be improved without sacrifying stability. On the other hand, high resolution in frequency measurements may call for very long sampling times thus making the measurements iconvenient. It is well known that in spectral-related methods the accuracy of measured parameters of sinusoids can be increased by interpolation, which may be turned into reduction of sampling time. The improvement achieved by interpolation depends on the signal-to-noise ratio of measured signal. In this paper an interpolation scheme is outlined and the analysis of noise sensitivity is presented. All calculations are verified by simulations and measurements. The practical implementation and real monitoring data are also given.

articleTitle: Functional Possibilities of the SMC Characteristics Monitoring of Electronic Apparatus by the Two-Frequency Probing Method
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The two-frequency probing method (TFP) belongs to the family of most informative and productive methods of controlling the susceptibility characteristics and the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of radio electronic devices, units and elements.

articleTitle: Circuit Shielding of the Digital Transmission Systems in Communication Cables
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Due to extended implementation of digital transmission systems problems of circuit shielding in cable lines has been studied in a wide frequency range. The issues of the shielding theory including electric and magnetic components have been developed. Interactive effect patterns between shielded circuits of symmetrical PCM cables are represented. The recommendations on the choice of shields for these cables are provided. The cable structures for PCM systems with transmission gain 60 - 70 dB are offered.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antennas on Metallic Cylinder Covered with Radially Inhomogeneous Magnetodielectric
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Microstrip antennas on circular conducting cylinder covered with a multilayered magnetodielectric are investigated. The general problem of radiation from a cylindrical multilayered magnetodielectric structure excited by an arbitrary volume current distribution is formulated and solved. The transmission line model for two coupled lines is employed within the radial function and axial function expansions approach. Radiation patterns and input impedance for coated wraparound microstrip antenna and microstrip rectangular patch are presented. Crosspolarisation arised from the coupling of different modes at the layers boundaries is especially discussed.

articleTitle: Correlated Current and Electric Field-Derivatives Emitted by Triggered Flashes
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Current (I) and current-derivative (dl/dt) measurements with submicrosecond time resolution were made on triggered lightning return strokes at the Kennedy Space Center (Florida) during the Summer of 1985 and at Saint-Privat d'Allier (France) during the Summer of 1986. The current was measured using a coaxial shunt and the current-derivative with a wideband inductive sensor. Both sensors were located at the base of the lightning channel and were connected through fast analog fiber optic links to several fast transient digitizers and a magnetic tape recorder. It was thus possible to record triggered lightning current variations over a large frequency range (I : DC to 30 MHz ; dl/dt : DC to 90 MHz). The peak-currents of the return-strokes varied between a few kiloamps. and 50 kiloamps. and the peak currentderivatives between a few tens of kiloamps/microsecond and 260 kiloamps/microsecond. Current measurements are of the same order as those obtained before; the main value of the peak-currents is about 14 kiloamps, corresponding to the main value of the peak-current-derivatives about equal to 100 kiloamps/microsecond. These direct current-derivative measurements are the first ones obtained so far. They are much higher than they were expected to be; this is the main result of the present work allowing better characterization of lightning current transitions. Electric field-derivatives were also measured simultaneously at close range from the discharge. Electric field-derivatives (dE/dt) and current-derivative (dl/dt) are roughly proportional. Assuming the "Transmission-line model", the lightning current velocity, obtained from the ratio of dl/dt and dE/dt measurements, has a mean value equal to 2,8 108 m/s. (s.d. = 0.4 10<sup>8</sup> m/s), which is about twice the velocity obtained by optical measurements [14]. One of the likely reasons is that the current propagation could be faster in the first tens of meters above the ground. Nevertheless, it is not yet understood how the lowest part of the lightning behaves: in particular, is there only one current propagating upward from the ground level?

articleTitle: Characterization of Harmonics and Electromagnetic Interference Generated by Plasma Torches
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The increased application of plasma torches in industry "has led to recent interest in characterizing the harmonics and electromagnetic interference (EMI) generated from these devices. Harmonics and EMI generated by high power plasma torches can affect the power, frequency waveform and the operation of microelectronic equipment. In order to mitigate these undesirable effects, it is necessary to have a thorough understanding of the noise's characteristics. This paper presents results from an investigation on harmonics and interference generated during plasma torch operation. Using a 3 MW ac three-phase plasma arc device in a series of laboratory tests, the voltage and current waveforms recorded at different points of the power supply system during torch operation have been analyzed by the Fast Fourier Transform technique. Odd harmonics of the power frequency have been observed up to 1 kHz and flicker in the range of 6-10 Hz has also been observed. The effect of axial plasma gas flow rate on the harmonic generation will be discussed. In the electromagnetic interference investigation, the transient and steady state electric and magnetic fields generated during start-up and operation of an 80 kW dc plasma torch have been recorded. The high frequency transient field generated during start-up has a significantly higher magnitude than the steady state field. Proximity effect has also been observed. Shielding and grounding techniques to minimize the effects of EMI from plasma torches will be discussed.

articleTitle: Noise and Intererence Measurement Techniques in Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper submits practical noise and interference measurement techniques in th "c" band satellite communication and gives practical application results when the earth stations are inside the electric substations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference in Low-Voltage Power Supply Networks
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of radio and pulse interference measurements are given in this paper. The results of measurements in residential area are shown in form of graphs, the other measurements is described as a difference from a residential area. It can be used for estimation of minimum necessary susceptibility of electronic devices, connected to the low-voltage power supply network.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Electromagnetic Compatibility between Large Thyristor-Fed Drives and Industrial Networks
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) between large thyristor fed drives and their networks and other consumers is very acute. In the USSR there are many industrial installations using large thyristor fed DC drives. The extensive theoretical studies and laboratory experiments have been made and corrective measures have been adopted for improvement of EMC between thyristor-fed drives and power networks of these installations. For evaluation of the adopted measures the experiments have been conducted to study the effect of contaminating the network of thyristor-fed drives and application of various facilities for EMC improvement at two 2000mm hot strip mills of two steelworks and a large compressor plant.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of Large Cranes as Unintended Receiving Antennas
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The prediction of currents and voltages induced on a large crane by an incident electromagnetic field is examined. The problem is solved in a virtually exact fashion by the application of the method-of-moments technique for solving the integro-differential equation for the current induced on the crane. Sample numerical results are given.

articleTitle: Bioeffects of Millimeter-Wave Irradiation on Hemopoietic System
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Bioeffects of milimeter-waves on the Hemopoietic system were studied which has been considered to be of great importance for EMC. In the in vitro study, it was found that after murine marrow cell suspension exposed to 36.4GH mm-wave field the CFU-C formation of BMC was greater than that of sham exposed samples, but difference on the connts of labelled BMC was not shown. In the in vivo study, it was found that mm-wave exposure could increase the peripheral white blood cell counts of mice and promot the recovering of CFU-C of the murine marrow damaged by Y-rays.

articleTitle: Calculation of Actual Screening Factors of Aluminium Sheath Cables with Plastic Cover
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aluminium sheath cables with plastic cover are widely used as a protetion measure. The protection engineer often assume that the aluminium sheath is supplied with equally spaced ground connections of equal resistance, but these assumption are not always satisfied. This paper introduce a method of computing actual shielding factor of aluminium sheath in case of unequally spaced ground connections of unequal resistance.

articleTitle: Multivalent Usuable Surge Generator for Tests According to CCITT-Recommendations of Series K
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes an universal surge generator especially for tests" according to CCITT-Recommendations of K-series. It is possible to turn between five operation modes (3 surge voltage wave shapes and 2 surge current wave shapes) by changing of special plugs and switchgers. Besides this fact the generator is suitable for automatic test processing.

articleTitle: Computer-Aided Methods for Frequency Assignment
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Rationality of frequency planning methods strongly affects the performance of radio communication system and its compatibility in given environment. A brief analysis of frequency assignment problem and its mathematical formulation is presented. Algorithmic methods are briefly discussed and a Monte Carlo optimization method is described.

articleTitle: Disturbances on a Medium-Voltage Supply System Caused by Harmonics-Measurement, Computer Simulation and Remedial Measures
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The presented network investigation supported by a computer simulation program will help to find in any given supply-system the reasons for high harmonic voltage-levels, which may cause faults or damages on connected equipment, and to study remedial measures. The method is demonstrated at a given highly distorted 20kV-supply-system and consists of the following steps: - simultaneous automatic measurement of harmonic voltages and feeder currents over a long period (at least one week); - Application of the correlation method to identify the system-parameters from occasional switching operations and natural variations of the load; - Proof of the parameters by use of different analysing methods and check of the parameters by synthetic methods which base on known equipment data; - Verification of a computer simulation by comparison of calculated and directly measured values; - Use of the computer simulation to study the effect of possible remedy measures by systematically varied system-parameters. The mentioned example turned out to be difficult since the only effective and realistic remedy seems to be the splitting into two separate systems, one feeding the industrial load, the other the household and commercial consumers. In future, other methods may be possible: A special compensator injects harmonic currents into the system and compensates flexibly the existing harmonic level by real-time processing of measured values.

articleTitle: Methods of Fourier Integral Operators in Diffraction and EM Waves Propagation
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There are methods making possible to obtain the results in the proximity of caustic. They are based on so-called problem microlocalization, i.e the considerations are transposed to a determined domain of the cotangent boundle.

articleTitle: Some EMC Problems Concerning the Shielding, Electric Filters and Grounding of Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An experimental nuclear magnetic resonance imaging system using a resistive magnet has been developed at the IMME CEPR SAS: the TMR-86. This paper is devoted to the solution of the basic EMC problems connected with the design and construction of electric filters and shielding cage, including the measurement of the shielding factor and grounding complex of the MR-tomograph.

articleTitle: Notch Fed Microstrip Antenna and Arrays
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An extended theory and practice on notch fed rectangular microstrip antenna and arrays are presented. The feed point is located in a notch along the centerline of the antenna length and the input impedance can be varied to match any source impedance by moving the feed point with depth of notch, without affecting the radiation properties of antenna. A method for the design of medium gain microstrip array antennas is described. A modular approach is utilized in which a given antenna is used as building block for higher gain antennas. Design equations sufficiently accurate to specify important design properties of the proposed antenna, and measured radiation characteristics are included.

articleTitle: The Calculation Flow of Multipoint Network System for Prediction of Earthquake Epicenter Locations and the Eliminating of Man-Made Noise Interference and the Source Mechanism of Emissions
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: As presented at the opening session of the last Wroclaw symposium on EMC. the authors are building the multipoint network system for the prediction of earthquake epicenter location by means of the seismogenic emission phenomena at around Tokyo area. The network system, is consisted of eight observation points with 50 km separation each other and each point set up a new digital type direction finding detector with two loop sensors tuned to 82 kHz. The output signals of receivers are added into digital vector composition circuit to obtain a direction angle of source point, and this signal is transmitted to center computer through telemeter line. To protect from local man-made noise interferences, the warning is only announced when the computation results of center computer have pointed one small area with high cross corelation values between all points data. The source mechanism of emission related precursor of earthquakes is to be explain as the rocks around focus area emitted electromagnetic emissions when they crashed completely by the distortion pressure. And this emission energies are propagated to ground surface along the boundary surface of fault as a surface wave mode and radiated from slit antenna which consisted of the boundary at ground surface of fault. Authors will present the comput flow and try to explain about source mechanism of these emission in this paper.

articleTitle: Coherency of Millimeter Waves in a Near-Earth Turbulent Atmosphere
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Results of theoretical and experimental studies of the near-earth turbulent atmosphere effect on the propagation of the millimeter band radiation are represented. A theoretical analysis two-frequency spatially-temporal mutual coherence function has been made under the assumption about statistical relationship of amplitude and phase fluctuations of the wave. In contrast with the earlier scientific publications this approach appears to be more common and takes into account the specific particularities of the millimeter band.

articleTitle: Diffraction from a Step Discontinuity in a Conducting Plane
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The scattering from a step discontinuity in a finite conducting plane is examined using the - geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD). Incidences of plane and cylindrical waves with the - plane of incidence normal to the step edge are considered. For plane wave incidence the observation points are taken at a constant distance - from the step edge. For cylindrical wave incidence the observation points are located in the far field region. Numerical results of the amplitude of the total field are presented for various incidence angles. It is shown that the - discontinuities present in the fields obtained - by geometrical optics (GO) are eliminated when the diffracted field is included.

articleTitle: The Probability of Lightning Strokes INTO High Voltage Substations in Dependence of the Arrangement of Air Terminations
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Lightning strokes into high voltage substations must be expected with a specific probability because of their square dimensions. Based on the theory of the electrogeometric model the possible arrangement of the air terminations is discussed. The application of the rolling sphere method is used to dimension the height of the ground wires and rods where the operational considerations for the arrangement are considered. On example of a new constructed 380/220 kV- substation the expected frequency of lightning strokes into the endangered parts is calculated at some diversified arrangements of the ground wires and rods. The variation between wires and rods is discussed on the technical point of view as well as on economic considerations.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Measured Electric and Magnetic Field Strengths around the Dipole Curtain Antennas at the PORI Short-Wave Station
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Theoretical and experimental results are presented for the assessment of RF hazards near dipole curtain short-wave antennas. Equivalent power densities for the electric and magnetic fields were measured and computed at different heights and distances in front of 2 × 2 and 4 × 4 element antennas, and the distances within which the exposure limits 10 W/m<sup>2</sup> and 2 W/m<sup>2</sup> may be exceeded were determined. The maximum environmental safety distance to multi-storey dwellings is about 1 km.

articleTitle: Some Propagation Characteristics of Electromagnetic Signals, on the Earth, from Lightning Discharges
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is very interesting to study the propagation characteristics of the electromagnetic signals which originate in a lightning discharge, We report on two years of observation of the propagation of such E M signals by measurement of a potential difference between two earth rods. A preliminary study indicates that the most interesting characteristic is the signal surface penetration over a wide frequency range. Lower frequency components enter deep into the earth so that the majority of signals have a spike-like appearance. The signals could only be detected at the suburban test sites.

articleTitle: Electric Field and Radio Noise from the Polish 750 kV Power Line
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The first 750 kV transmission system was put into service in Poland in 1985 after commisioning tests. The 750kV system on the Polish territory comprises the 750 kV overhead power line of a length of 114 km and an electric power substation 750/400/110 kV provided with two sets of 750/400 kV autotransformers each rated at 1250 MVA. This transmission system is mainly, intended for the supply of electric energy from the USSR to Poland, Czechoslovakia and Hungary.

articleTitle: A Comparison between Small-Aperture Polarizabilities and Coupled Coaxial Dipoles with Application to Near-Field Shielding-Effectiveness Measurements
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The near-field shielding effectiveness of a material may be measured by placing it between two closely spaced dipoles (electric or magnetic) and noting the resulting insertion loss. However, this approach is difficult to implement in practice. An alternative method is to cover an electrically small aperture with the test material and measure the resulting loaded aperture polarizability (electric or magnetic), as is done in the dual transverse electromagnetic cell. This approach is straightforward, but may not intuitively appear to be a near-field shielding effectiveness simulation. Expressions are developed and discussed herein which relate these two configurations. Experimental data are used to verify the utility of these results.

articleTitle: The Influence of Lightning Current in the Channel on Voltages Induced within the Buildings which are Struck by Lightning
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper an attempt was taken to investigate the problem as to influence of lightning current in the channel between the building roof and clouds on the values of magnetic fields inside the buildings.

articleTitle: The Expectations of the Consumer Regarding Signal to Noise Ratio Versus Standard Testing Practice
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The basic problem, which is the compatibility between different installations, means that it is necessary to judge whether compatibility does or does not exist. If one looses sight of the original aim, this judgement can result in something which does not contain information on whether equipment is compatible with "the real world” or only with artificially fixed limits adapted to laboratory environments. I am going to address mainly this problem.

articleTitle: Analytical Considerations in a Statistical - Empirical Interference Prediction Model for Mobile Radio Environment
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The signal interference situation in a landmobile radio environment has been modelled using a statistical approach. The paper describes the analytical structure of the model for Poisson - distributed interferes in a limited geographical area The probability density function (pdf) of the expected signal-to-interference ratio is computed by combining pdf-s of different parameters involved. Probability that this ratio is below a threshold is computed to obtain the statistical description of the interference in a mobile radio environment.

articleTitle: An Approach to the Calculation of Currents and Potentials Induced along two Parallel Underground Conductors with Finite Length by External EMF Effects
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper, a new approach, which could be used to calculate the currents and potentials along two parallel underground conductors with finite length induced by external electromagnetic fields, is first presented on the basis of Maxwell equations, theory of differential equations, and relative references. Arbitrary terminal impedances connected to the earth and interaction between conductors have been taken into account. Universal solution, and examples for some special case are given.

articleTitle: Remarks on the Program
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: U.R.S.I. comes first on the list of cooperating organizations, and I noted with pleasure, that both my successors as chairmen of Commission E of U.R.S.I. are organizing a session here. Professor Kikuchi was responsible for the session on Ball, bead or Anomalous lightning and EMC. Egely starts his survey with the remark, that ball lightning belongs to the few'phenomena on earth, whose fundamental principles are not understood, and even near the end of his thorough discussion of the anomalies. There is not on known method of energy transport, which could be responsible for the observed phenomena. In the contribution by Ohtsuki and Ofuruton obtained more then 2000 cases of ball lightning in Japan, confirmed an experiment by Barry, that produced a long-lived ball lightning phenomenon at atmospheric pressure in a low density hydrocarbon gas, and also by discharge of a capacitor bank in a cotton aerosol (lifetime 0.85 sec). Dijkhuis discussed ball lightning from a quantum-mechanical point of view, and came to the conclusion, that a collapsed vortex core of self-trapped electron pairs supplies enough power for a ball lightning. He hopes to develop a small scale fusion reactor based on ball lightning.

articleTitle: Protection against Danger and Disturbances of Electromagnetic Origin in Telecommunication Network
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Disturbances in telecommunication network and installations can have many causes. One of these is the influence of the electromagnetic fields that are generated in different processes. The generation of such fields and their disturbing effects in telecommunication network was early observed. It was the natural sources of disturbances in telecommunication circuits that were noticed first and foremost the atmospheric discharges. Later another type of natural disturbances was observed and caused by geomagnetic storms. By the increasing number of electricity lines and installations in the vicinity of the telecommunication systems other types of disturbing effects were observed. We got the man made sources of disturbances that were caused by the capasitive, inductive and conductive coupling including direct contact between the electric power and the telecommunication systems. Other types of man made sources of disturbances were radiation from RF-transmitters and emission from different electronic devices. By introducing more sensitive electronic equipment often electric power supplied, the mains power and the telecom network will be more and more "connected" to each other. For these reasons a growing number of environmental parameters have to be taken into account concerning both emission and immunity severities to solve the EMC problems nowadays.

articleTitle: Analysis and Synthesis of Filter Structure for Rejecting EM Interferences BY Automatic Geophysical Data Processing IN Real Time Scalling
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: During geophysical data processing operations many mathematic and technical difficulties are caused by a great amount of EM interferences in registered signals. That is why during automatic data processing operations the largiest part of the computer memory can be loaded by unnecessary information which leads to the growth of time and material expenses during production of final results.

articleTitle: Effective Gradients of the Refractive Index of AIR in Continental Regions
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents the results of the determination of effective vertical gradients statistic distributions of the refractive index of air obtained by a radiotechnical method under the specific conditions of sharp continental climate in Central Yakutia, Transbaikalia and South-East Mongolis. The registra - tion of field tensity v/as carried out in decimetre and metre range on the route from 36 km to 54 km in length in every climatic region in the period of May to September with simultaneous registration of meteoelements vertical structure from special masts.

articleTitle: Proximate Analysis of Electromagnetic Compatibility of Radio Equipment through Discrete Models of Interference Situations and Fast Fourier Transforms
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Step by step analysis of inadvertent radio disturbances in which in a successive manner a number of stages such as amplitude analysis, frequency analysis, detailed analysis are carried out, is becoming largely popular in the practice of analysis and provision of EMC of radio electronic devices. Most of the difficulties arise, when non-linear phenomena in the receiver with a large number of input signals within a broad dynamic range, are analtzed, especially in case of intermodulation analysis. The predominant approach to this problem is the one based on the use of a spectral line model of the interference situation at the input of the receiver and its sections, receiver model in the form of a standard radioelectronic element, non-inertia and non-linear, or as a combination of such elements, as well as very complicated combinatorial relations for calculating the products of intermodulation of separate narrow-band components of the input effect at the initial non-linear stages of the receiver.

articleTitle: Biological Effects Related to e and h Vectors of Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There are consensual opinions on the contribution of E vector and controversial opinions on the contribution of H vector to the biological effects of e-m fields. Under the influence of the same frequency E and H fields of 8 kHz, 45 kHz or 41 kHz with intensities 6000 to 9000 V/m and 70 to 210 A/m the growth retardation, weight changes of anterior pituitary and adrenal glands, reduction of Na+ and K+ contents in the hypothalamus, and increased conductivity in brain cortex were found in rats exposed to such fields repeatedly for 20, 22 or 45 days. The majority of these changes were more pronounced under the influence of H field than of E field. These results support the reason to use two orders magnitude of impedance E/H in standards for both HP and LF e-m fields.

articleTitle: Interaction of Low-Intensive Microwave Radiation with Biological Objects
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is presented the systematization of experimentally established main characteristic features of interaction of low-intensive microwave radiation with biological objects (flux density low than 10 milliwatt/cm<sup>2</sup>). It is shown that biological effects of microwaves are privilegy of trickly organized, complicated livinig biological objects. Biological objects are divided in non-depending on frequency of radiation and frequency-depended (resonant). The frequency-dependend bioeffects are divided in two parts: the first one included effects, where resonant properties are exhibited on atomic-molecular level, the second one includes effects, where the dependence on frequency is due to the properties of propagation of millimeter waves in bioobjects (for example, the appearance of a standing electromagnetic wave in layer-structure, Fabri - Perrot resonator, dielectric resonator, parasite resonant circuit, combined with emitting antenna, etc.). The role of water molecules in reception of millimeter radiation is discussed, and the application of microwaves for investigation of intra-molecular interaction in liquid (biological) matter. In conclusion the medical aspects of application of microwaves are considered. It is shown, that this radiation nay be used in therapeutic aims for restauration of disturbed function of organism.

articleTitle: Time Domain Analytical Solution of Multiconductor Transmission Line Problems
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the derivation of analytical expressions for transients in lossless lines loaded by linear non-reactive elements and excited by interfering disturbances. The telegrapher's equation model is adopted and the equivalent circuit of the n-conductor line is shown to be valid for both internal and external sources. Crosstalk is accounted for via the coupled equations of the line while the external interference is represented by a source of electromagnetic waves. Closed-form solutions in the time domain are derived, and therefore no numerical inversion of Laplace transforms is required in the solution process. Our results, besides being directly applicable in many practical cases, provide an insight into the electromagnetic mechanisms of the interferences and constitute a valid check for more complex all-numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Spacecraft Electrostatic Discharges on Geosynchronous Orbit
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Geosynchronous satellites are permanently submitted to inpingement of energetic electronic and are immersed about one tenth of the time in a hot spacecraft charging plasma, in kilovolts range. Electrostatic discharges can cause anomalous behaviour by interference on electronic circuits. A lot of effort and resources were dedicated by Space Agencies to solve this problem. In this paper the ESA experience in the geostationary orbit environment is presented and the charging processes and the used prediction numerical codes are re-called. The electrostatic discharges and their coupling effects to the satellites electronic circuits ar analyzed. The ESA study programs in this domain and the project guidelines are presented.

articleTitle: Suppression of Harmonic Currents in HVDC Bulk Transmission Lines and Networks
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An effective means of suppressing harmonic currents in long-distance overhead HVDC power transmission lines can be smoothing devices that are connected to short-circuited sections formed by earth wires. The parameters of such smoothing devices (SUT) are selected to compensate completely or partly the series inductance of the respective earth wire circuit at the frequency of the harmonic to be suppressed. The principal advantage of the SUT is that its components are not affected by the operating voltage or current, which makes them simple in design, reliable in operation and comparatively inexpensive. On the Ekibastuz-Centre UHVDC line the SUTs are applied to suppress the principal 12th harmonic in the earth. Their connection to the terminal sections of the line makes it possible to cut communication line modifications costs by a factor of three and more. In multiterminal HVDC schemes use of SUT on intermediate substations does not appear practical because the costs of communication line modifications are only 20% lower.

articleTitle: Scaling Law for Fusion Power from Boson Vortex in Ball Lightning
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A break-down analysis for air is presented in which the electric field drives electron concentration inside the region of thermodynamic instability caused by exchange interaction between free electrons. We assume that electrons in unstable region form pairs subject to Bose-Einstein statistics. From Feynman's equation for a charged superfluid a steady-state vortex solution is obtained with self-confined electron pairs in the bosonic core. Radial electric fields are screened out by ions circling around the negative vortex core. Relativity theory sets an upper limit for energy storage in the vortex structure which is consistent with reported ball lightning energies. Ions with different charge-tomass ratio as in air acquire relative kinetic energies above the threshold for fusion reactions between light nuclei. The usual Gamow tunneling cross section for fusion leads to linear scaling of fusion power with energy stored in the vortex structure. With deuterium concentration as in humid air the proposed fusion process provides sufficient power to support a high-energy ball lightning

articleTitle: The Theory of Arbitrarily Oriented Dipole Antenna over a Lossy Half-Space: High-Contrast Approximation
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electric field integral equation for the current on arbitrarily oriented dipole antenna radiating above a lossy half-space is solved by the method of moments, with the interface effect included via the high-contrast approximation. The relative accuracy of this approximation is examined.

articleTitle: VHF/FM Frequency Planning Constraints
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper is devoted to the initial, or so-called frequency-distance constraints (FDC) in frequency planning. The method offered is based on terrain database usage. New ideas are realised in zone of coverage prediction, as well as in FDC determination. Many assumptions, leading to inefficient frequency planning, are ignored: in the FDC determination process, the frequency is the only unknown characteristic of every future transmitter station (TS). The comparatively insignificant influence of the frequency over the propagation in the VHF/FM band is shown. The method is relevant to in-band constraints computation but can be easily adapted to out-band FDCs.

articleTitle: The Research of Microvawe Propagation above 10 GHZ in the Troposphere
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: System of collecting and processing data propagation above 10 GHz was developed. This system consists of radiolinks 11 GHz and 18 GHz, earth to satellite link of 11 GHz and automatic system for collecting and processing time data. This paper also shows the first measuring results.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Atmospheric Interference Effects on Control Systems
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Nowadays, when control circuit with sensible electron devices are widespread and lightning protection reduces fire and health hazards to negligible proportions. it is avident that evaluation of the 1ighting interference effects on control systems comes into prominence. Precise determination of these effects is difficult, not only because of randomness of lightning parameters and complex configurations of coupling circuit, but because of nonlinear nature of input impedances in the investigated control circuit, as wel1. Therefore the simplitied evaluation methods, treated as a development of the methods presented in [l], are proposed in the paper, These simplified computations methods concern interference sources in the nature of a pulse, e.g. lightning discharges and the interference effects occuring in the control systems, e.g. ones fitted up in a building, The suitable equivalent shape of the source pulse, which approximates ones existing in nature due to lightning discharges, is, used in the, computations, The results performed for the wide range of parameters of the lightning discharges and the interfered control system are reported in the paper.

articleTitle: Interaction between EMC of Telecommunications and Technical Methods of Transmission to Increase Noise IMMUNITY
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Owing to the development of the electronics of discrete semiconductor technology into an integrated technology the hazard - free and/ or disturbance - free operation of devices, installations and systems under the influence of external electromagnetic fields has become an essential factor /1/ /2/.

articleTitle: Cross Polarization Reduction in Pyramidal Horns
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper addressee the problem of crosspolarization in pyramidal horns with the objective of identifying the source of cross polarization in this important class of microwave antennas and hence means of its reduction. It is found that the source of cross polarization are currents on the internal surfaces of the horn walls· A cross polarization reduction technique that is suggested is to cover the Internal surfaces of the walls with some absorbing material. Experimental investigations confirmed the validity of this technique. A reduction of 6.5 dB in cross polarization was achieved using this method.

articleTitle: Exact Time-Domain Transmission-Line Equation for Two-Conductor Line and its Solutions
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: the voltage and current transmission line equations in the time domain are obtained from the Maxwell equations, we found immediatly that the voltage equation accord with the equation which was deduced by the classical method, calling the quasi-static method. it also means that there is no remarkable different between the voltage equation when we use the quasi-static approximation, but the current equations are quite different. Here, the authors give out the semi-infinite length transmission line as an especial example and obtained the rigrous response of the voltage and current of the lines which are drived by a step pulse.

articleTitle: Statistical Characteristics of Dynamic Range of Inadvertent Disturbances with Space-Scattered Grouping of Their Sources
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To assess the efficiency of the performance of radio devices under the conditions of inadvertent radio disturbances it's important to foreoast the dynamic range of interfering input signals in the receiver. This parameter of an interference situation, which is understood as the ratio of the level of the most powerful input signal to that corresponding to the receiver’s sensitivity in the main channel, is directly related to the danger of inadvertent disturbances along the channels of spurious reception and non-linear effects - intermodulation, blocking and crossmodulation distortions; it i made use of as the basis for establising appropriate levels of test signals at a multisignal testing of the receivers aerial susceptibility.

articleTitle: Constructions of Algorithms for Hybrid Reflector Antennas Pattern Calculations and Real-Time Beam Steering Control
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Reflector antennas with feeding antenna arrays (FAA) are of great concern at the present time. These hybrid reflector antennas (HRA) allow to effect the sharp spot beam continuous steering into limited sector. To achieve this purpose it requires nonlinear variation of FAA amplitude-phase excitation and makes insufficient procedures commonly applicable to phased arrays.

articleTitle: Susceptibility and Vulnerability of Radioastronomy in the EMC Environment
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Man-made interference of various kinds has an increasingly negative impact on observational astronomy. Many, if not all radioastronomical observing sites have experienced some types of effects degrading the observations. Those observatories which have not been affected yet too much, will be in the foreseeable future, while many of the sites with negligible effects at present, will become under severe pressure in the coming years. Planning for present and future radioastronomical observations must take these serious problems into account. A strategy to coordinate European and worldwide action is proposed.

articleTitle: Radirefraction and over the Horizon Propagation of Microwaves in Conditions of Polar Troposphere
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The report presents the research a statistical characteristic results of radiometeorological parameters of polar troposphere surface land layers. IT is shown that the temporary regularities of the radiometeorological parameters cause to a greater extent the seasonal variations of the radio signal levels over the horizon paths in the polar climatic conditions. In order to get basic regularities of the field the experiments were carried out on the two multytopped distant paths with 357 and 261 km. long in range of decimetre waves. A standart machine was used by measuring. The gains of the using antennas are equal to 42-46 dB. The signal registration lasted day and night during the year. The instant values of the fluctuating field were registered every three hours of the 30 minite session. As a result of statistic treatment of 5-minutes average values of signal levels, integral distributions of attenuation factor are constructed for every season. Experimental integral distributions of average values of attenuation factor for every path subdue satisfactory to a logarithmic normal law. First the seasonal variations of the field was discovered and investigated at the distant troposphere propagation paths with winter macimum and summer minimum. This fact is in close correspondence with the seasonal variation of N in this area. The report also reveals with the mutual correlation coeffcients between radioclimatic parameters and signal levels which are necessary to foretell conditions of electromagnetic compatibility of radioelectronic means by the investigation of radiofields in the polar troposphere. It is obtained that this coefficients of correlation are equals 0.7-0.8 in winter and 0.3-0.4 in summer on boths paths.

articleTitle: Satellite Observation of Equatorial VLF Noises and the World-Wide Distribution of Thunderstorms
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Ariel 4 satellite VLF data are used to investigate the characteristics and generation (propagation) mechanism of equatorial VLF noises. Equatorial emissions are defined as vlf noises whose mean (running mean during ~30 sec) intensity exceeds 40 dB above 4.8×10<sup>-19</sup> W m<sup>-</sup><sup>2</sup> Hz<sup>-1</sup> (free space equivalent) in the magnetic latitude range less than 30°. They are found to be located in longitude to the centres of thunderstorm occurrence and they show a similar seasonal dependence to that of thunderstorms. Also the character of emissions is impulsive and the observed mean/minimum and peak/mean ratios are condequently high. Hence the equatorial vlf emissions as observed by Ariel satellite have been found to be well explained by assuming thunderstorm generation. Many of the characteristics can be attributed to D-region absorption and propagation in the ionosphere and lower magnetosphere.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Wire Broadcasting; Telephone Communication and Discrete Data Circuits on AIR Communication Lines
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper Deals with requirements for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of different circuits on air communication lines. Practical recommendations on parameters for wire broadcasting, tele-mecanic, data transmission signals and spacing of circuits on the poles are represented. The present paper is the last in series of studies on EMC in local communication lines. The results of studies on low-frequency interactive effects between discrete and analog information circuits of urban telephone network cable lines were reported at the 4-th Symposium on EMC (Wroclaw, 1978). The results of EMC studies on transmission of the discrete information in local communication cable lines at a higher frequency range up to 64 kBit/s were reported at the International Symposium on EMC in Zuitzerland (Zurich, 1982) The present work represents the results of studies on EMC in discrete and analog information circuits of local telephone network air lines.

articleTitle: Spectra of Signals in Coherent in Coherent X-Band Navigation Radars
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of investigation of clutter return in coherent X-band navigation radar, operating at sea environment are presented. The experimental conditions include different polarizations of incident radiation, sea states and low grazing angles. The correlation between received amplitude and instantaneous Doppler shifts of clutter return is demonstrated. The differences between spectra at horizontal (HH) and vertical (VV) polarization are discussed - the spectral moments at HH has generally greater values than at VV. It is shown, that the contribution of receding scatterers in clutter spectra is not as large as those reported earlier by other authors. Frequency spectra of backscattered signal are obtained with improved coherent equipment and digital system for data recording and spectral analysis.

articleTitle: The Transient EM Fields Produced by the Short DC Transmission Line
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The space distribution of the electromagnetic field caused by the short currents which propagate along the direct current line is discussed in this article. The vector results of electric and magnetic field are given. The earth considered is perfectly or imperfectly, respectively and is semi-infinite with homogeneous. The DC line is infinite and is no dissipation or with small dissipation. The theory of image is used in this article. The final results are given in frequency domain.

articleTitle: Multi-Band High-Resolution Spectrum Monitoring System for AM and FM Signals
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A high-resolution system for frequencies below 30 MHz was introduced at previous EMC Symposia. The extended-range, LF-UHF band measuring system can be formed by cascading the appropriate receivers. All the advantages of the narrow-band signal analysis can be retained for FM signals as well, if - besides of the linear translation - the signals are also divided in frequency. Due to the frequency division, the wideband FM transmission become narrowband signal and the carriers can be directly identified and their frequencies can be precisely measured by interpolation in the spectra. In the paper the measuring set up is described together with real-life measurement results.

articleTitle: Measurement of Intermodulation Distortion in SSB Radio Transmitter Power Amplifiers with Narrow Band Noise
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper are presented the results of measurements of the intermodulation distortion of the transistor linear power amplifier. For measuring the intermodulation distortion, two methods were employed, namely the standard two-tone method and the narrow-band noise signal method. The comparison of both methods gives rise to the statement that the narrow-band noise signal method does better represent the amplifier operating conditions and that the so-called noise intermodulation distortion coefficient describes the radio-frequency interference produced by the transmitter more accurately.

articleTitle: Influence of Environmental Buildings on land Mobile Radio Fading Characteristics
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the result of measurement of land mobile propagation fading characterstics on 460 MHZ and 900 MHZ band in China. Statistical analysis of the measurement data confirmed that the fast fading envelope of mobile radio receiving signal does not always follow Rayleigh distribution.
