But M distribution and Log—normal distribution can give a better description. The conclusion could be used to improve the EMC analysis in frequency management system or mobile radio system design.

articleTitle: Mathematical Studies on Mutual Inductances between Crossing Lines with Earth-Return
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper, the author studies the mutual inductances between crossing lines with earth-return. the terminal effects from power lines are taken into account. By applying complex image method, universal and analytical solutions to the mutual inductances are first derived. Examples and curves are given, and the results of computation are in good agreement with the experimental regularity.

articleTitle: The Influence of Metal Sheath Earthing of Telecommunication Cables on the Core-Sheath Voltage by a Direct Lightning Stroke
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the lightning EMC of a telecommunication cable, the insulated metal sheath of which is repeatedly earthed at certain points. A mathematical model has been developed to calculate the core-sheath voltage by a direct lightning stroke. The results of calculation for typical earthing arrangements of two types of cable in different soil resistivities are presented by plotting the peak core-sheath voltage against the magnitudes of the lightning current. The significance of results for solving the lightning protection problems is discussed.

articleTitle: Measurements of Vertical Radiation Patterns of VHF/UHF Broadcasting Antennae by Means of a Helicopter
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The new oryginal measuring method of vertical radiation patterns for VHF/UHF broadcasting antennae by means of a helicopter is presented in this paper. Measurements are performed during ascending flight at a small angle and then results are processing by a special computer system. This method makes it possible to avoid the interference of the ground-reflected wave. Results of measurements of a TV Antenna operating in the IV frequency range are presented.

articleTitle: Study on a Measuring System of Electrification Interference to Track Circuit
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In recent years, more and more Electrification railways have been built in China and even more Electrification railways will be coming in for using. In the Electrification section, the propultion corrent becomes stronger and stronger along with the increase of weight propuled. The propultion current(PC) is a big interference source for track circuit of railway signaling(TCRS). As we know, track circuit plays an important role in railway automatic control system of signaling. It is a channel in which control information is transmited. But if the information of the TCRS is smeared by the PC, the safety and the efficiency would go down. That is why we have to do our best to survive automatic section system and TCRS, by moans of EMC theory and method. In this paper the EMC measurement of interference in TCRS from PC is discussed. Emphasis is put on high performance of the measurement system analysis and a method of getting unbalance current between two rails.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) in Automotive Electronics
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An increasing number of electronic devices has been introduced into vehicle design. This made it necessary to consider the environmental conditions. According to investigations the mechanical, thermal and electromagnetic conditions in the vehicles are often extremely hard. According to vehicle measurement results carried out at the University of Engineering of Zwickau a lot of influences cause interferences at susceptible electronic devices. Therefore, investigations about EMC are necessary for application of complicated, electronic systems such as antiblocking system (AB8) or board computers. EMC must already be considered at the stage of design of a device. It is a quality factor of electronic products. According to the international standardization the EMC on vehicle electronics is divided into three parts /1/: - Intra-system interferences between the electric or electronic subsystems (Intra-System EMC) - Interactions between the operator and the electronic equipment in the form of electrostatic discharge (ESD) - External system interactions with reference to emitted radiation interferences by electric or electronic system of the vehicle and the radiation influence of the vehicle electronics by irradiated interferences (Inter-System EMC) Thus, in principle, there are conductive and radiation interferences. Because of the effects the conductive interferences can be divided into interferences on the supply lines (board network) and signal lines. Interference sources produce interference signals. These can cause a temporary malfunction or even permanent damage to the electronic equipment if the interference level is higher than a definite unity. International standards about the electrical transients along supply lines were established, further are being prepared.

articleTitle: Investigation of Correlation and Spectral Signal Characteristics on Crossing Path Propagation
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The spatial-temporal statistical characteristics of the coherent signals recepted on two crossing directions have been investigated. It has been confirmed experimentally, the correlation takes place between phase fluctuations in the result of the turbulent atmosphere influence in the crossing directivity diagram region. The phase fluctuation spectral analysis results and the registered near crossing region retraction index fluctuation statistical analysis results are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Capacitance Loads Antennas and Decrease of Reradiators Effects
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Linear dipole of considerable electrical length with lumped loads, included to create a required current distribution and to provide (on a wide frequency range) high matching with cable while radiation is maximum in the direction, perpendicular to the dipole axis, is considered in the work. Considerations, based on the theory of impedance dipole with surface impedance, variable over the length of the dipole are presented. Curves of propagation constants' variations over the dipole and the corresponding values of loads, meeting the requirements, are determined. It is shown that there is a decrease of effects of neighbouring metal objects at the same time.

articleTitle: Analysis of Ball Lightning Observations
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Ball lightning is a rare natural phenomenon, but there are already more than 3000 written observations. Analysis of the time and site of formation shows that it is ostensibly a nonlinear electric effect requiring very high energy and electric charge far beyond our present laboratory parameters.

articleTitle: Methodical Aspects and Practical Problems Connected with Students' Training on Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) training structure in Universities arrangements of lectures in the courses on different instruction levels and the contents of these courses are suggested. Practical realization of the suggested training model and its perspective development are discussed in accordance with the concrete conditions, in a given University and speciality.

articleTitle: Monolithic Dielectric Filters for EMC Applications
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We propose here a method to design monolithic dielectric filters (MDF) for achieving new levels of performance towards EMC applications. The filter consists of a high-permittivity dielectric slabs placed in a waveguide below cutoff loaded with low-permittivity dielectric slabs. These filters are miniature, high selective, with low losses and small level parasitic resonances.

articleTitle: The Propagation of Long and Middle Radiowaves in Mountain Paths of the Southern Siberia
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper contains the results of measurements on the module of wave attenuation function |W| at frequences of 50,236,281 and 576 kHz and local values of the surface impedance in the mountain and forest path for a distance of 600 km. The object of researches is the experimental study of long and middle wave propagation in highlands and the estimation of accuracy for predicting wave attenuation function based on local geophysical characteristics of the uppermost ground under complicated natural conditions of Southern Siberia.

articleTitle: Correlation between Terminal Interference of an Artificial Mainsnetwork and Disturbance Voltage in Mains
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents attempts of the author to estimate moduli of impedances of arbitrarily selected, real power supply networks within area of town Wrocław. The impedances have been estimated both for symmetrical and asymmetrical components of interference voltage. A network coefficient k<inf>s</inf> was introduced. It makes possible to estimate the level of interference voltage in real network for both symmetrical and asymmetrical components when the voltage characteristics of a disturbance source, measured on the terminals of the artificial mainsnetwork, is known.

articleTitle: An L-Band Fractional-Helix Antenna for GPS Portable Receiver
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An L-band multi-element fractional - turn resonant helix antenna has been analysed and designed for the GPS portable receiver. The presented antenna is an electrically small (e.g. 0.3λ-axial length and 0.18λ in diameter), provided circular polarization over a broad angular region and near cardioid-shape radiation pattern. This paper will discuss the antenna relative to its performance in a satellite communication system, its electrical and mechanical characteristics as a single antenna. Integral formulas for the radiation of the antenna have been derived and computed by numerical integration and found to agree with the measured data.

articleTitle: Prediction of near and Far Field Patterns for Shaped Dual-Reflector Antenns by using SNFGTD Method
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Both near and far fields of a shaped dual-reflector antenna is predicted rapidly and accurately by using the SNFGTD method(1),(2), the computed result show good agreement with the measured data. In addition, A new method to calculate disastrous field value round an antenna is presented in terms of SNFGTD, which is an effective technique for solving the EMC problem related to an antenna.

articleTitle: The Earthquake-Induced IGW'S in the Ionosphere F Layer
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In relation to an important problem of accounting large-scale travelling ionospheric disturbances exerting direct influence on the both earth-ionosphere waveguide and F region parameters in the VLF range, the problem of the earthquake-induced internal gravity waves (IGW's) in the ionosphere F layer is solved· The possibilities of the IGW's generation by both the volcanic eruptions and the manmade explosions are discussed.

articleTitle: Discharge Morphology Causing EMR and Technologies to Suppress the EMI
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The actual condition of EMR generation in plasma reactors, which employ a bridged-streamer corona and/or repeated-spark discharge for NO<inf>X</inf> and CO<inf>X</inf> treatment was clarified. Some ideas for suppressing the EMI are proposed by standing on the control of discharge morphology.

articleTitle: Rayleigh, Rice and Nakagami - in Search of Efficient Models of Fading Radio Channels
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Fading radio signals are usually modelled by the Rayleigh distribution; Rice’s model is also sometimes used. The versatile Nakagami model is rarely resorted to. Here, merits of the latter are confirmed by recently obtained in Poland simple solutions to interference and error-rate problems. The channel model derived from Nakagami distribution is recommended as the efficient tool for system-oriented theory and practice.

articleTitle: Distributions of Extreme Values of the Radiorefractive Index
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents some results of studies of the large scale radio refractive Index distribution In the north of Poland. The statistical relationship of the radiorefractivity profile was examined from the point of view of radiometeorological parameters. Statistics of monthly probability values x<inf>ij</inf> of exceeding of preselected thresholds of radiometeorological parameters were Investigated. So were the distributions of extreme values of radiometeorological parameters.

articleTitle: Discussion of Standard Antenna Method and its Improvement
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the problems in relation to standard antenna method (25- 1000MHz) i.e., the determination of the RF voltage measurement, and the calibrated AUT. An improvement on the RF voltage measurement is obtained by using an additional short-circuit line.

articleTitle: Resonant Action of External Electromagnetic Radiation on Nonlinear Processes in Biomacromolecules
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Effects of action of low-intensity microwave radiation are considered. These effects were studied for a number of years in research groups of many countries. The possibility is shown of resonant action of external microwave radiation on the processes on energetic transport in biological macromolecules. It is shown, that effects of resonant action of external microwave radiation are essential for a model processes of propagating excitations in alpha-spiral protein molecules in form of solitons, i.e. propagating local pulses covering several peptide groups. These effects arise even at low values of external radiation (10 milliwatt/cm<sup>2</sup>), and may affect on the processes of energetic transport in alpha-spiral structures, which are in great amount in proteins of neurons surface, being in charge of susceptibility and transformation of signals. The resonant frequency of soliton excitation appeared to be different from the own phonon frequeny of quasi-one-dimensional biomolecular chain: <tex>$\omega\sim\sqrt{{\rm v/c}\omega_0}$</tex>, where v – the velocity of sound in a substance, c - light velocity. It is presented also the review of known mechanisms of resonant action of microwave radiation on biological objects.

articleTitle: EMF Measurements below 100 kHz
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Nowadays a set of protective standards for frequencies below 100 kHz is being discussed and they will be implemented in the near future. It has created a demand for appropriate measuring equipment designed for national sanitary and radio inspections as well as for other services. Many phenomena may be used in design of electric and magnetic field sensors. Their sensitivity, however, does not meet requirements. The only way to obtain required sensitivity is to use a combination of small electric and magnetic dipoles. The concept is the least convenient from the point of view of other parameters. The work presents a brief theoretical baseground of VLF EMF metrology as well as short presentation of designed meters and probes. The probes may be applied together with an old MEH type DC voltage monitor. The new concept of the meter in which an antenna is integrated with voltage monitor and power supply makes it possible to limit influence of mutual couplings between a probe and a DC monitor, field disturbances caused by a meter and unstabilities created by electrostatic charges.

articleTitle: Development of a High Strength Electric Field Sensor
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the details of a system of sensors developed to measure electric fields during susceptibility testing of systems exposed to high field strength environments. The system operates in a section of the S band at field strengths up to 25,000 volts per meter. It measures and records peak field strength and signal waveform, and is responsive enough to accurately record pulse width and pulse repetition rates for pulses as narrow as one microsecond. The sensors are small and self contained, and are connected to the measuring and recording system by optical fiber cables. The system design technique can be used to produce similar systems tailored to other frequency ranges and field strengths with simple changes in sensor design.

articleTitle: Nature of Ball Lightning in Japan
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The data of eyewitness of the ball lightning in Japan obtained by "Japanese Information Center of the Ball Lightning (fire ball)" is analysed. We can conclude that the Japanese ball lightning differs from the continental one reported in Europe and the United States, which shows a special nature of ball lightning in the southern, very hot, and humid island. We also make a report on the experimental production of the ball lightning in a hydrocarbon gas and other aerosols.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Discharge by the Travelling Field
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electrostatic discharge is generated at the surface of a solid by a traveling field even though it takes only short time. Discharge and ionizationon near the surface of a solid have an effect of charging up the solid which is called as field electrification. Moreover, this discharge make the hazardous radiation field. Usually, the velocity of a traveling field is high and the capacity of the surface of a solid is small, and the spark gap of electrostatic discharge is nallow. So, these discharge are very much sharpe, and the radiation field should be polarized according to the charge distribution. This phenomenum should be considered as a function of field intensity, solid shape, and dielectric constant. Experiments showed this to be powerful and hazardous for electronics.

articleTitle: EMC-Analysis Engineering Methods
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper suggests engineering methods for determining the EMC (Electromagnetic Compatibility) parameters of a Radioelectronic System (RES) using a simulation model, on the basis of originally worked out EMC-analysis approach.

articleTitle: Radio Noise and Noise Suppression Method in Breaking Silver Contacts under DC. 10 ~500 Volt’s Sources and 0.01~110 a Currents
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Although the voltage applied between contact-electrodes of the electromagnetic relays is generally in DC.12 ~ 48 volts, there are recently relays which their voltage are as high as 300~400 volts, as wells. When these relays break, various types of discharges appear between the contacts. These discharges radiate electromagnetic interference waves. Thus, using the relays with Ag contacts and an equipment with Ag contacts, we carried out the experiments under conditions of DC. 10~ 500 V, 0.01 ~ about 10 A, resistive load and in air. As the results, the discharge diagram was made in V-I plane, and a non-quasi-discharge region with lower noise level was found in about(0.1 ~ 0.3)A. At last, methods for suppressing the noise caused by discharges were described.

articleTitle: A New System to Decrease the Lightning Interference Caused by Magnetic Induction on the Aerial Low Voltage Line
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Until now the major cause of lightning interference on the aerial low voltage line has been believing by most engineers in this field. So they have made mainly their efforts to gain the arrester which has the characteristic reducing the over-voltage to lower than the withstand value of the lines and other apparatus.

articleTitle: Means of Reducing the Electric Field Intensity and the Electrostatic Induction on Vehicles near High Voltage Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The design parameters of an overhead transmission line are chosen in the USSR so as to meet "Sanitary Norms and Regulations on Protection of the Public" which limit the maximum electric field intensity at 1.8 m above the ground to 10 kV/m at crossings of 330 kV and above lines with motor roads and to 15 kV/m in uninhabited areas. When the requirements are met the current flowing through a person at a contact with a standard motor vehicle generally does not exceed the safe 5 mA value. The KAIF-82 program was used for computer calculations of the effectiveness of various means of reducing the electric field intensity and the elect - rie induction on motor vehicles, such as a greater conductor height, grounded shielding wires under conductors, transport corridors formed, for example, by rows of trees planted under the line, a closer phase and subconductor spacing at crossings of lines with motor roads, crossings of lines with motor roads at angles close to 90°, and some others. The main method of electric field control is to raise the conductors higher above ground. To meet the above-mentioned norms, the distance to ground must exceed by 4 to 7 m that selected by the dielectric strength of the air gap alone, which means a much higher cost of the line. Grounded wires under each phase of the line make the induced currents and voltages on vehicles 20-30% lower; however, the effectiveness of the wire shielding drops rapidly with distance from the line. A 6-8 m wide transport corridor formed by two rows of 4-6 m high trees makes the field and the induction on vehicles four times and more as small. A larger width and a smaller height of the corridor lessen the effectiveness noticeably. Even a single row of trees was shown by the calculations to be an effective means of electrostatic induction control if trees are 2-3 m higher than vehicles. When the overhead line and the motor road cross at a right angle and when the length of a vehicle is comparable to or exceeds the phase spacing and the conductor height, the induced current and voltage on vehicles drop sharply because of compensation of the charges induced by adjacent phases, of the line on the surface of the vehicle. The field and the induction can be lowered considerably by bringing closer the subconductors of the bundle and by reducing the phase spacing (e.g., by substituting V strings for I strings) in the overhead line span crossing the motor road. Rational selection of design parameters of overhead lines is the most effective and economical means of reducing the electric field intensity and the electrostatic induction on motor vehicles near overhead lines.

articleTitle: Measuring methods for EMI - Testing According to CISPR22 Recommendation
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Computing devices and other similar digital equipments have been recognized as the most serious interference sources to TV and sound broadcasting systems. CISPR 22 established a test method for international use for measuring radio interference generated from these kinds of equipments. This paper deals with the measuring method described in CISPR 22 from the viewpoint of automatic testing and examines EMI test instrumentation including the test receiver or spectrum analyzer. First of all the characteristical differences between the two detectors used, quasi-peak and average are discussed. Further, a brief comparison between the videoaveraging and digital-averaging methods for spectrum analysis is made. Finally practical suggestions are made to simplify testing and to speed up the whole measuring process.

articleTitle: Estimation of Electromagnetic Compatibility of Antennas
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility

articleTitle: EMC in Amateur Radio of Japan
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There are many interference on EMC problems in the field of amateur Radio. At the last three years, one of the largest interference problem which appeared in Japanese Amateur Radio is "TELEPHONE I". Modern Japanese telephone service system has been changing quickly to the multiple service system. The home and office telephone can be used as the interphone, the home security control operation and etc., and they can controlled from outside place through telephone system. But these new type telephone equipments are used the high impedance microphone and headphone, and installed the IC and LSI and micro processor elements in the digital circuit system. These non-linear circuits are often mis- operated by the interference of radio waves from Amateur Radio Station. In this paper, I describe the activities about the organizing committee on the interference control and protection of the Japanese Amateur Radio League and the protection research on the new type "TELEPHONE I" interference.

articleTitle: The Noise Immunity of LS Series Nand Gates
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the dynamic noise-immunity characteristics of LS series NAND gates, which are the basic components of most popular integrated circuits (IC). Noise immunity is observed for the number of noise-applied-inputs and for the fall time of noise, experimentally. It is concluded that noise immunity deteriorates with the increase of the number of input terminals in the case that fall-time of noise is short, and gets near the static noise immunity in the case that fall-time of noise is long. In second experiment to get the background of the above noise immunity characteristics, the frequency-impedance characteristics (Abbr. f-Z CH.) between inputs and ground, between power supply and inputs, and between power supply and ground are measured. As the results, f-Z CHs between two terminals of LS series NAND GATES have capacitive characteristics, the impedance across two terminals becomes small with the increase of the number of inputs, and hence, inputs have differentiation characteristics. Finally, the equivalent circuit is proposed from the view point of noise.

articleTitle: Criteria of Efficient Spectrum Use and Frequency Planning
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Due to a rapidly increase of the spectrum loading by emissions of various radio systems more and more attention is presently given to activities which would lead to improving the efficiency of the spectrum utilization (ESU). To fulfil these tasks it is necessary to have reliable ESU criteria. This paper presents an analysis of the existing ESU criteria with the aim of their classification which is in line with the whole process of frequency planning.

articleTitle: Two Theories of Horn Antennas
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic compatibility of radio systems to a considerable degree is determined by the radiation characteristics of their antennas.

articleTitle: Concept of an Electromagnetic Pulse Laboratory
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The concept of an Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Threat Laboratory equipped with various system for EMP susceptibility testing is presented. The methods used in this study can be divided into two major classes: field simulation and injection. In the injection method, a pulse generator is connected directly to the input terminals of the object under test. The pulse generator simulates EMP-induced currents and voltages that will be picked up by a feeder, cable or circuit. In the field simulation method, the pulse generator is connected to an EMP simulator. The electromagnetic environment produced should be as close as possible to the actual threat.

articleTitle: A Method of Considering Directional Properties of Antenna Systems in Choosing Optimum Slot-Type Screens Parameters
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a further development of a previously suggested by the authors graphical and analitical method which consists in choosing optimum values of slot-type screen parameters intended for local suppression of interfering fields.

articleTitle: EMC and EMP Considerations in an Industrial Plasma Processing
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Plasma processing of new materials becomes increasingly important in various ceramic and semiconductor industries, as well as metal industry. In this work, three different types of plasma processing and their EMC and EMP considerations are proposed and discussed in detail. These three types of plasma processing are: I. Low pressure plasma processing — this included capacitive and inductive RF power supplies and microwave power supply; II. Thermal plasma processing — this included ignition circuit of plasma torch, electrostatic discharge (ESD) from powder injections, and RF and microwave plasma torches; III. High pressure low temperature plasma processing - this included corona discharge noise - AC and DC, and EMP generation from pulse discharge.

articleTitle: The Cross Polarization Decoupling of Antennas in the Difraction Propagation of Centimeter Waves
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The work presents the results obtained by an experimental investigation of a spatial structure of the electromagnetic field under the shade of obstacles on the main polarization and its cross component when there are various modes of wave reemission polarization. The experiments were carried out on the paths having dominating obstacles of the mountain and hill terrain in the 10 cm range of waves.

articleTitle: An Automatic System for E-Field Sensors Testing in the Frequency Range 20 HZ - 18 GHZ
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes an automatic system developped by Aeritalia EMC team to calibrate field sensors in the frequency band 20 Hz - 18 GHz. For frequencies lower than 250 MHz a T.E.M. cell is used. At higher frequencies the EM field is generated by pyramidal horns inside an anechoic chamber. The automatic system is used to calibrate Aeritalia sensors and to measure antenna near field gain.

articleTitle: Frequency Characteristics of Electricity Supply Net Work Impedance
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Determining frequency characteristics of electricity supply network impedance appears very helpful for estimating compatibility of various power systems and devices: /e.g. the inconveniences caused by thyristor converters operation to centralized remote control systems/ and for verifying the harmonics filtration efficiency. The knowledge of the frequency characteristics of impedance is an inevitable precondition for complying with Czechoslovak Standard ČSN 33 3430 The Rules for Electric Appliances from the Point of View of Influences on Electric Power System.

articleTitle: Far Sidelobes Decreasing Possibilities for Scanning Beam-Producing Antennas
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Pattern far sidelobes level is one of the paramount electromagnetic compatibility parameters for receiving and radiating antennas. Leading to pattern sidelobes level decreasing common recomendation is making falling down to edges or special electromagnetic field distribution on an antenna aperture. It is hard to realise this recomendation because of resulting electromagnetic field distribution difiera from exciting distribution through edge and interaction effects. These effects lead to increasing pattern far sideiobes level. Aspiration to decrease influence mentioned effects leads to necessity of making excities strongly falling down to edges or to change excities according to scanning angle and to provide the required electromagnetic field distribution on an antenna aperture. As a result or the first case it is necessary to increase aperture sizes for providing requirement gain, and in the second case it is necessary to complicate exciting scheme.

articleTitle: The Numerical Analisis of Transient Electromagnetical Excitation for Conducting Slab
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Solutions for transient electromagnetical excitation problems have been of particular interest for recent twenty-thirty years. One of the various branches of research where transient problems are present is EMP interaction and coupling analysis. These problems play an important role in development of radar and communication systems with application of transient or nonsinusoidal (noise - like, Walsh function, code function, e.a. waveforms) electromagnetical waves. It is shown, that these systems give some advantages in comparison with classical concept - application of monochromatical waveforms.

articleTitle: Interstitial Applicators for Microwave Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic characteristics of linear interstitial applicators radiating into biological media are analyzed, together with the associated thermic distribution, in order to achieve an e.m. power deposition into deep tissues. Moreover it is shown that arrays of such applicators may realize a prescribed temperature pattern. The theoretical results are compared with experimental temperature distribution on phantoms by infrared thermography measurements.

articleTitle: Long Term Alterations of EMI Caused by Home Entertainment Electronic Devices
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of electromagnetic interference /EMI/ brought about by encreased radiation of home entertainment electronic devices /HEED/ due to some ageing effects, unqualified repairments, home made "improvements" etc. Simulation investigations of several types of TV receivers, home computers and other electronic devices have been performed. Measurements have shown that the increase of radiation due to the above mentioned phenomena may exceed 40 dB in comparison with the newly bought device of the same type.

articleTitle: Absolute Intensity of Whistlers as Deduced from the Direction Finding Measurements and its Latitudinal Variation
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The absolute intensity of daytime whistlers at low (geomag.lat. 25°) and middle (35°) latitudes has been studied on the basis of the data with the field-analysis direction finding system. At low latitude, the maximum absolute intensity is estimated to be 250µV/m, while the corresponding maximum intensity at middle latitude amounts to 600µV/m, being about 2.4 times that at low latitude. This latitudinal variation of daytime intensity is interpreted in terms of the joint influence of (a)source activity, (b)magnetospheric propagation effect and (c)ionospheric transmission loss. It is found that whistlers at each station are attributed to ducted propagation in the magnetosphere and have exited the ionosphere close to each observing station, as determined by the direction finding results. Furthermore, the cloud distributions observed by satellites have yielded that the duct entrance point of whistlers at each station falls within the active thunderstorm region. Hence, we can conclude that daytime whistlers are originated in the active thunderstorms in each conjugate region, are trapped in ducts and followed by nearly the vertical exit from the ionosphere at each station. Finally, the latitudinal difference of the intensity is satisfactorily interpreted in terms of the difference in the ionospheric transmission loss on the assumption of the same source intensity at each conjugate point and of no amplification in the magnetosphere.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Mining Data Measuring Systems
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper considers problems of electromagnetic compatibility in making up a mining data-measuring system (MDMS) operating under sparkle-, explosible conditions. The problem of implementing local computer networks (LCN) utilized for controlling and monitoring technological processes under mining and other operational conditions hazardous in gas and dust explosion, requires working out of special circuit engineering solutions, securing safe operational conditions.

articleTitle: The Noise Radiated from Showering Noise
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The circuits which include inductive loads are accompanied with showering noise at its contacts opening. This paper clarifies the generation Mechanism of showering noise, referring to frequency-impedance characteristics of inductive load. The noise radiated from showering noise is considered as induced voltage of near-field, and it is clarified that radiated noise is made up of voltage noise (capacitive coupling noise) and current noise (inductive coupling noise) by getting the experimental data of noise characteristics induced on adjacent contact to driving contact (which drives inductive load) of multi-contact relay. Finally, based on the experimental data, we make mention of radiated noise reduction method.

articleTitle: Survey of Methods for Calculating the Induced Voltages and Currents in Practical Cases Given in Volume II of the Directives /1988 Edition/
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The rapid development of new technologies in telecommunications, electric power transmission and distribution, and electric railway systems has made the earlier issue /1963 edition/ of the Directives of the International Telegraph and Telephone Consultative Committee /CCITT/ out-of-date and this former issue is therefore being updated completely. The new Directives /1988 edition/ are divided into a series of separate /nine/ volumes, each dealing with a particular part of the complete subject. In this paper the main principles of Volume II /”Calculating induced voltages and currents in practical cases”/ are described. Modern calculation methods which are suitable for computer techniques have been incorporated in Vol.II

articleTitle: The Nearfield of Paraboloid Antenna
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The knowledge of nearfield of paraboloid antenna is important in the design of compact rang soure reflector and for the protection of those people around a transmitting paraboloid antenna. The age old Concept-Fresnel's zone is used in this paper for calculating the nearfield of paraboloid antennas. Compared our result with the results by spherical expansion and GTD, the agreement is excellent. This shows that the basic physical concept and simple mathematics can also solves complicate diffraction problems.

articleTitle: Radio Astronomy and Frequency Protection Problem
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A snort description of the basic instrumental and astronomical limitations facing Radio Astronomy is given. It is shown now these problems have been solved and now spectacular are the achievements up to the present. Radio Astronomy has grown fast and became an unique research branch of modern science both in the instumental and observational sense. It has at least equal or brighter prospects for the future. With the most sensitive detection techniques available now it is more than ever necessary to provide Radio Astronomy with quiet spectral regions. We are now threatened with new dangers that may make Radio Astronomy observations impossible. Some suggestions are made how to make these threats less dangerous, yet one should bear in mind that the best cure is prevention. An appeal should be made to all the active users of the radio spectrum in an effort to prevent the extinction of Radio Astronomy.

articleTitle: The Measurement of Cross Modulation Interference of dual Frequency Transmitter
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The technique and method of measurement of cross modulation interference of dual frequency transmitter, the one of measurement items in Electromagnetic Interference(EMI), is described. The theory and process of measurement and connection of measuring system are included in the paper. It also pays more attention to the processing of data and analysis of residual modulation noise in quantifying test. The work is different from MIL-STD-462A CS05.

articleTitle: Analysis of Digital Signal Detection Algorithms Resistant to Electronic Environment Changes
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An analysis is presented of optimal algorithms for quasidetermined signals detection against narrowband stationary Gaussian noise at a different capacity of an a priori information about power and statistical characteristics of signal and noise.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of the Buildings Steel Construction against Impuls Magnetic Fields Caused by Lightning Strokes
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The introduction of electronic devices in measuring-, controlling-, and regulating systems on the one hand increase the possibility of operations but on the other decrease the susceptibility these devices to impuls magnetic fields. This fact caused that now more often in design of lightning protection of buildings it must be taken into account the protection of electronic devices which are working inside the building. In many cases one of the way for this purpose is to increase the number of wires in which the lightning current flows to ground and often the steel rods of building's construction are used for this purpose. In this paper the shielding effectiveness of building's steel constructions against magnetic fields was considered in two cases when the lightning struck - in the corner or in the other points on the outside parts of the roof - in the vicinity of the buildings. Theoretical calculation were made in arrangements in which the length of the steel rods was much bigger than distance between them. These investigations were used to estimate the current distribution in multiconductor systems and the current induced in these systems when the lightning struck in the vicinity. Thanks to the knowledge of these currents it was possible to calculate the values of magnetic fields inside the buildings and compare these values with the field which is caused by lightning current in the channel.

articleTitle: An Automatic Measurement of the Arrival Polarization of Whistlers
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An analogue equipment is developed and described, which can automatically identify and track the magnetospheric whistler signal so that we can measure the amplitude ratio and phase difference between two horizontal magnetic field components of each whistler over a wide frequency range (5 to 2kHz) and then we can study the ionospheric transmission characteristics of whistlers. Whistler is a very low frequency (VLF) electromagnetic wave originated ir the lightning in the opposite hemisphere and propagated through the magnetosphere, and is a gliding tone such that the wave frequency decreases with time; i.e. T=df<sup>-1/2</sup> (T:time, f: frequency and D is a constant called "dispersion" determined by the plasma parameters along the propagation path)<sup>1</sup>. In order to study the propagation mechanism of whistlers and also to deduce the magnetospheric density from dispersion values, it is of great importance to determine experimentally the region where whistlers emerge from the ionosphere. This is the so-called "direction finding (DF)". We have developed the field-analysis DF method based on the simultaneous measurement of two horizontal magnetic and one vertical electric field components<sup>2,3,4</sup> which is made at a specific point frequency around 5kHz where we expect the maximum energy in the whistler spectrum. The problem is to know whether the results of direction of arrival and polarization measured at the particular frequency can be generalized to a wide frequency band. The extension of our DF system to a wide frequency band is a difficult task to be done, but it is being planned<sup>5</sup>. Instead, the frequency dependence of the characteristics obtained only from two horizontal magnetic field components is studied in this paper, which provides an useful insight to the ionospheric transmission properties of whistlers<sup>2,6,7</sup> Namely, when the amplitude ratio and phase difference of the whistler signal on the crossed loop aerials show no particular frequency dependence, we can infer that the whistler characteristics (direction of arrival and polarization) do not depend on frequency. On the contrary, when the polarization characteristics of the whistler vary with frequency, the direction of arrival will be different at different frequencies for the relevant whistler.

articleTitle: Corrosion Effect of EMI on the Buried Pipeline
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: On the metal surface of Daging-Qinhuangdao petroleum pipeline in China, many pits 2—5 mm deep were discovered. The cause of this pitting is considered as the electromagnetic interference(EMI) effect of power lines. The pitting corrosion only develops at points, where the electrical field intensities are very high, which we have called field intensity corrosion. The pipeline EMI can be classified into continual, twinkling and intermittent interference according to AC corrosion.

articleTitle: Computer Support of Frequency Planning
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The frequency spectrum is an irreplaceable resource and future development of all radio communication services depends on its effective exploitation. The most important problem in frequency planning of these services is the achiev- ment of their EMC in the scope of the suggested service or network as well as with regard to other frequency spectrum users. At the present stage of development of radio communications this problem has become so intricate that its solution is unthinkable without computer support if the requirement of maximum economy is to be satisfied. Computer application makes it possible either to solve partial problems, or to develop a complex computation system permitting full-scale approach to the solution of the problems in connection with EMC and effective utilization of the frequency spectrum. Admittedly, the former method offers quick solutions to the most urgent problems, but with time it tends to result in confusion and duplicity in the solution of numerous problems. The latter method, on the contrary, may be more timeconsuming, but i t s advantage is in systematic approach to problem solution, unified recordkeeping and simple work for users who are specialists in the radiocommunications field, but inexperienced in the work with a computer. This way was chosen by P. & T. Research Institute in Prague resulting in the development of a computer -supported system for radio-communications frequency planning called MAKRO, the description of which is the subject of this paper.

articleTitle: Sources of Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) in Converter-Fed Rolling Mill Drives
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with voltage/current spectral characteristics in electric circuits of basic components and- devices as EMI sources of converter-fed rolling mill drives. The mill drive's components are represented as equivalent electromagnetic emitters in the nearest space zone. The theoretical and experimented levels of E-field and M-field strengths as well eus their vectors in the surrounding space are given.

articleTitle: On the New Idea of a Radar for Ground Flash Location
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new idea is presented on the location method of the strike point of ground flash using a radar with a phased array antenna. The wave length of the radar must be 10 cm or longer than it. This new location method is recommended to be used as a complementary method to another conventional one.

articleTitle: Closed-Form Approximation to the Bounded Part of Exact Kernel of Cylindrical Antenna Integral Equation
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A computationally efficient closed-form approximation to the hounded part of exact kernel, partitioned after Schelkunoff, of cylindrical antenna integral equation is given. The approximation together with the existing elliptic integral representation of the singular part effectively obviates numerical integration in the evaluation of the kernel. Sample results obtained from the method-of-moments solutions are given to validate the approximation.

articleTitle: An Update on PLHR and its Effect on the Environment
publicationTitle: Ninth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Since the Ariel 3 and 4 mapping of the zones of power line harmonic radiation (PLHR) in 1967 and 1972 two important events have occurred. Firstly, the Soviet Union annual electrical energy production (AEEP) has increased at such a rate that it exceeded that of the USA (1967) in 1984 and will have attained the USA (1372) level in 1987. Therefore if, as seems reasonable, the Soviet PLHR is related to AEEP, we might now expect a significant contribution to the formation of the Electron Slot. Secondly, Armstrong (1987) has found direct evidence of magnetosphere/atmosphere coupling such that the precipitation of energetic electrons (>20kev) may trigger lightning discharges when the meteorological conditions are appropriate. This gives support to a suggestion (Bullough et al, 1980; unpublished) that the secular increase in thunderstorm activity in southern Canada (Changnon, 1977) may be due partly to increased PLHR and associated particle precipitation. The Soviet PLHR may be having a similar effect.
